TriPhysBench: Evaluating Physical Intelligence for Embodied Agents

TriPhysBench: Evaluating Physical Intelligence for Embodied Agents

Zhongxiang Sun、Chenghao Yang、Haojie Ding、Boheng Zhang、Fan Yang 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Embodied agents need physical intelligence to understand their surroundings through physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning. These capabilities must work together to interpret events and make quantitative judgments. Existing benchmarks advance physical understanding and general-purpose tool use, yet the coordination of these capabilities in physical scenarios remains insufficiently characterized. Inspired by Popper's Three Worlds, we introduce TriPhysBench, a benchmark of 410 questions from 200 videos that brings physical perception, physical knowledge retrieval, and physical reasoning into a shared evaluation setting. Its measurement-grounded and knowledge-grounded subtasks impose complementary demands on obtaining observations and acquiring external specifications, then applying them to quantitative problems. Among six representative vision-language models, the best achieves an answer accuracy of only 50.38%, revealing limited performance on tasks that require these capabilities to work together. We further introduce TriPhys, a framework that learns a unified policy for physical perception, knowledge retrieval, and quantitative reasoning from complete tool-integrated trajectories. The policy uses intermediate reasoning to guide retrieval and computation, then incorporates tool feedback into subsequent physical inference. On 110 questions from videos excluded from training, TriPhys improves answer and solution scores across three Qwen configurations, with a 17.7% relative gain in answer accuracy for TriPhys-27B over its Qwen3.6-27B backbone. This work provides a benchmark and a learning pathway toward embodied agents that move beyond recognizing events to understanding and reasoning about the physical processes behind them.

PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making

PlanContext: Benchmarking In-Context Driving Decision-Making

Ruikai Li、Naiyu Gao、Hao Shan、Yizhe Fan、Yanhao Wu 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Real-world driving requires context-aware decision-making. Existing end-to-end driving benchmarks primarily assess trajectory quality through safety, compliance, comfort, and driving progress, leaving context-dependent decision-making insufficiently characterized. To fill this gap, we present PlanContext, a benchmark for evaluating in-context driving decision-making. PlanContext constructs paired evaluations by varying high-level driving intentions while keeping the observed scene fixed, enabling a natural and controllable assessment of context-dependent decision-making. We further define six representative driving contexts and jointly evaluate contextual decision correctness, road compliance, and dynamic safety with class-balanced metrics. Experiments on 9,561 scene-condition instances from NAVSIM and 23 public end-to-end driving models show that high conventional driving-quality scores do not consistently correspond to strong route-level in-context driving decision-making. Further analysis shows that model behavior varies with decision timing, road structure, and traffic interaction depending on the decision required by the current context. Our results highlight in-context driving decision-making as an important complementary dimension for evaluating end-to-end driving systems.

Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation

Evaluating Depth-Augmented Visual Features for Cross-Dataset Lunar Traversability Estimation

Jan Baturo、Bartosz Ptak

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Autonomous mobility is essential for sustained lunar surface operations, as communication delays and line-of-sight occlusions limit continuous teleoperation. Although recent traversability estimation methods increasingly rely on deep learning, the domain gap between terrestrial analogue environments and real lunar terrain can limit their generalisation, and real lunar traversability labels are scarce, making fully supervised training difficult. To address these challenges, we build a weakly supervised framework trained on sparse pairwise annotations and study whether augmenting visual features with depth-derived geometric information: depth, surface normals, and combined geometric descriptors. We evaluate the models in both in-domain and cross-domain settings using two terrestrial analogue datasets and the real lunar Chang'E PCAM dataset. Contrary to expectations, we find that naive geometric augmentation yields no consistent improvement over a strong visual-only baseline in either setting, with effects small relative to seed-to-seed variance. Instead, the choice of training source emerges as the dominant factor in transfer quality: models trained on domain-relevant sources transfer substantially better to real lunar imagery than the geometric fusion strategy improves any single model. Our evaluation runs onboard a resource-constrained edge device and provides a controlled baseline for designing more expressive multimodal fusion architectures in future lunar perception systems.

Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort

Resampling-based batch reweighting for ComBat harmonization of MRI radiomic features in a multi-scanner glioma cohort

Rifa Sajda Tasnim、Yushuf Sharke、Md Forhad Hossain、Rakibur Rahman、Enamul Hoque Bhuiyan 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Radiomic features derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are sensitive to scanners; therefore, they require harmonization across scanners. In a radiomic feature dataset, some batches may be severely underrepresented compared to the others e.g., the Erasmus Glioma Database, which may provide harmonized features biased towards the larger batches in the dataset. We investigated whether reweighting underrepresented scanner batches before empirical-Bayes ComBat estimation improves feature harmonization and reduces residual scanner association while retaining grade-related information. In this retrospective, the Erasmus Glioma Database included 733 eligible patients acquired at a single center across nine vendor-by-field-strength configurations. Structural MRI acquired at 1 T, 1.5 T, and 3 T; four structural MRI sequences were analyzed. From four structural MRI sequences, 428 features were computed using an IBSI-compliant PyRadiomics implementation. The sample sizes of some scanner batches were very small compared to others, which may produce unequal precision and shrinkage of batch-effect estimates. We proposed a data augmentation approach to overcome the limitation of ComBat. We provided exploratory evidence, along with confirmatory Kruskal-Wallis tests with a Benjamini-Hochberg correction to assess the proposed method. Before harmonization, 392/428 features (91.6%) differed significantly across scanner batches (median eta-squared=0.463). Standard ComBat reduced this to 13/428 (3.0%), whereas batch-augmented ComBat reduced it to 8/428 (1.9%); the median residual effect size was <0.001 for both harmonized conditions. Batch augmentation appeared to be a useful strategy to improve the performance of ComBat for feature harmonization under severe batch-size imbalance.

Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification

Spectral-spatial vision test-time training for hyperspectral image classification

Xiang Zhao

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification requires the representation of contiguous spectral signatures and spatial context under limited labeled supervision. Vision test-time training (TTT) offers an alternative to fixed-weight token mixing by performing self-supervised inner-model updates on the input sequence, but its application to center-pixel HSI classification remains insufficiently characterized. We present ViTTT-HSI, a spectral-spatial adaptation of the vision test-time training (ViT3) architecture. A spectral-aware embedding stem extracts ordered-band information using spectral convolution and forms spatial tokens without reducing their spatial resolution. Two ViT3-based TTT encoder blocks perform patch-conditioned token mixing, followed by the fusion of center-pixel and neighborhood-average features for classification. We evaluate the framework on Indian Pines, Pavia University, Salinas, and Houston 2013 using ten random seeds and dataset-specific training fractions of 1% or 5%. The mean overall accuracies are 97.6390%, 98.8753%, 99.3292%, and 98.4283%, respectively. Ablations reveal a substantial contribution from the TTT inner update on Indian Pines and a smaller positive contribution on Pavia University, while the relative benefits of the spectral stem and feature fusion depend on the dataset. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using patch-conditioned vision TTT for spectral--spatial HSI classification and highlight the role of the inner adaptation mechanism.

ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization

ASCoR: Asymmetric Semantic-Spatial Learning for Remote Sensing Domain Generalization

Zitong Wang、Shuchang Lyu、Meng Li、Qiang Wang、Guangliang Cheng 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 ⭐ GitHub 开源

Source-only domain generalization (DG) for remote sensing semantic segmentation seeks reliable predictions in unseen domains without target-domain data during training. Although vision foundation models offer transferable knowledge, category recognition remains sensitive to source-specific visual cues, while task-specific adaptation may weaken pretrained transferability. We propose ASCoR, an asymmetric semantic-spatial framework built on SAM3. Its text-conditioned semantic branch uses class-name prompts to provide explicit category guidance. Probe-Once Dynamic Adaptive LoRA distributes a fixed adaptation budget across encoder blocks to limit source-specific specialization. A complementary task-specific dense branch learns multi-scale spatial representations using a separate frozen SAM3 image encoder. A lightweight reliability router integrates the two branches through bounded spatial correction based on local prediction reliability. All components are trained using source-domain supervision only. Experiments on the ISPRS, LoveDA, and OpenEarthMap benchmarks cover nine cross-domain transfers. ASCoR achieves a state-of-the-art mean IoU of 68.61% across six ISPRS transfers, outperforming the previous best method by 2.69 percentage points. It also achieves the best results on all three LoveDA/OpenEarthMap transfers, with 59.07%, 47.95%, and 49.38% mIoU on Rural-to-Urban, Urban-to-Rural, and Urban-to-OpenEarthMap, respectively. Ablation studies, feature visualizations, and spatial reliability analyses support the effectiveness and complementarity of the proposed components. Code: https://github.com/WangZitong42/ASCoR.

EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation

EO-Jev: Decision Model for Earth Observation

Mohamed Atef Abouelhadid、Diaa Addeen Abuhani、Muhammad Akhtar Munir、Fahad Shahbaz Khan、Salman Khan 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Earth observation (EO) workflows require selecting among known outcomes, estimating confidence, and processing large volumes of imagery. Generative vision-language models can address these tasks, but autoregressive decoding is computationally costly and their confidence estimates are unreliable. Decision models offer an alternative, returning probabilities over candidate answers in a single forward pass. However, their accuracy, calibration, and transfer across EO tasks remain insufficiently understood. We investigate these properties through a diagnostic study of d3-flash (8.4B parameters) across 30 settings from 23 public EO benchmarks. We find that compositional reasoning transfers well and calibration improves over its Qwen3.5-9B backbone on 24 settings, while counting, change quantification, damage grading, and absent-object recognition remain challenging. To address these limitations, we adapt d3-flash through low-rank fine-tuning on public EO training splits, producing EO-Jev. EO-Jev improves significantly over d3-flash on 26 of 30 settings and matches or exceeds specialist references on 20 of 28. It also achieves an average gain of 8.0 points across 12 held-out settings and lower expected calibration error than specialists on 21 of 28 settings. These improvements come at a modest cost of 1.8 points in general decision performance. Our results demonstrate the potential of adapting general decision models into competitive EO generalists while highlighting persistent challenges in quantitative perception, option-order consistency, and calibration under distribution shift.

Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization

Fuse To Align: Multimodal Representation Learning for Retrieval via Hypergraph Regularization

Anindya Nag、Ambuj Mehrish、Sebastiano Vascon

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Multimodal retrieval must integrate complementary evidence from views that may be missing, noisy, or unequally informative. When a sample provides limited reliable evidence, learning from its views alone can hinder the acquisition of useful retrieval representations. Semantically related training samples may provide complementary observations, yet existing volume-based objectives jointly align modalities within each sample without explicitly enabling information exchange across samples. We therefore propose a training-time hypergraph fusion framework that connects observed modalities both within samples and across semantically related samples, allowing representation learning to draw on evidence beyond an individual sample while leaving the retrieval pipeline unchanged at inference. The framework includes HyVol as a special case and introduces two configurations: wHyVol learns view contribution weights and symmetric semantic affinities, whereas wRHG additionally models typed interactions and participant roles through relational propagation. Missing modalities are omitted rather than imputed, and the hypergraph is discarded after training, incurring no additional inference cost. Experiments on eleven zero-shot video-text and audio-text retrieval benchmarks demonstrate broad improvements with both GRAM and HyperGRAM. Across 17 video benchmark-modality settings evaluated in both retrieval directions, wRHG outperforms GRAM in all 34 comparisons and HyperGRAM in 33 of 34. Mean text-to-video R@1 increases from 63.4 to 68.2 with GRAM and from 64.8 to 68.4 with HyperGRAM, while the largest video-to-text gain reaches 13.3 percentage points on ActivityNet. Under missing-modality evaluation, both weighted configurations retain positive text-to-video gains over GRAM across seven benchmarks at every evaluated missingness rate, even when 90% of clips lack one modality.

Air-Scan-Based Point-Spread-Function Estimation for Megavoltage CT with Flat-Panel Detectors

Air-Scan-Based Point-Spread-Function Estimation for Megavoltage CT with Flat-Panel Detectors

Seemeen Karimi、Joseph Bendahan、K. Aditya Mohan

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Accurate spatial-resolution characterization of flat-panel detectors at megavoltage energies is difficult due to long-tailed cross-talk. Conventional measurements at high energy using line-pair gauges or knife-edge phantoms require expensive, carefully fabricated objects and precise alignment, and despite these, scatter from the phantom, detector, and imaging room can further confound the measurement. We present a method for estimating the detector point spread function (PSF) from the mean noise power spectrum (NPS) calculated from repeated radiographs in air. The approach is mathematically equivalent to an autocovariance-based method but is more practical for long-tailed PSFs. We validate the method using simulated air data and Monte Carlo N-particle (MCNP6) calculations of energy deposition in a flat-panel detector. We show that deconvolving the experimental PSF increases the accuracy of transmission radiographs of step wedges. The method requires no phantom or alignments and is straightforward to reproduce.

View optimization in Computed Tomography

View optimization in Computed Tomography

Seemeen Karimi、Christopher McGuire

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Many emerging CT imaging applications must operate with data from sparse projection angles, on the order of 10 views, such as first responder scenarios, dynamic imaging of detonation events, and flash imaging of materials under extreme conditions in high energy-density science. Few-view imaging is a data undersampling problem, that degrades tomographic reconstructions with streaks, shadows, and other aliasing artifacts, due to ill-conditioning. In few- view CT, the specific set of projection angles can strongly impact reconstruction quality, and the optimal angles depend on the object being scanned. Despite a surge of recent research, there is much to explore in this problem. We present an object-aware performance prediction framework for few-view projection datasets based on a matrix decomposition of the discretized forward model augmented with expected object gradient information. The method yields a quantitative score for a candidate set of view angles that can underpin a view selection recommendation algorithm. A key feature is that it can be applied at multiple stages of acquisition: a priori, before any radiographs are taken, or adaptively, after some radiographs are collected, to determine the next best view. We demonstrate the approach using simulated CT data with 5 view and 15 view configurations. Preliminary results are encouraging; images reconstructed using a standard statistical algorithm show that reconstruction accuracy agrees with our performance score. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated against a known ground truth using an information theoretic score. Continued testing with complex objects and multiple geometries is necessary.

Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) is critical for medical image segmentation as it adapts a model to an unlabeled target domain without accessing source data, thereby preserving data privacy. However, its effectiveness is often limited by confirmation bias: self-training models tend to miss small polyps, hallucinate foreground, and produce imprecise contours. We propose MedRT-SFSeg, a real-time SFDA framework built on a dual-head one-to-one/one-to-many YOLO segmentation architecture. Mask-DHF fuses precision- and recall-oriented predictions into stable pseudo-instances, while DURR uses the sign of pixel-level dual-head disagreement as a directional cue to expand or shrink masks, and additionally recovers missed instances and suppresses hallucinations. Seg-MARD further regularizes feature representations through mask-guided, region-stratified sampling. Experiments on bidirectional adaptation between Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB show that MedRT-SFSeg achieves 80.43%/80.77% Dice and 5.53/8.44 mm ASD, improving the non-adapted baseline by 7.7 and 9.8 Dice points while running at more than 62 FPS end-to-end. These results suggest that segmentation-aware dual-head supervision can improve pseudo-label quality without sacrificing real-time inference. Project page: https://danielnguyen-05.github.io/MedRT-SFSeg

Mahmoud S. Mayaleh、Liban Ali Achkir、Nijat Mehdiyev、Ahmet Ozdil

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Lip reading plays a crucial role in applications such as speech recognition, assistive technologies for the hearing-impaired, and biometric authentication. However, performance often degrades when the speaker varies and when certain speech sounds are visually similar. To address these challenges, we propose LipLingo, a robust lip-reading system based on the LipNet architecture, enhanced with a standardized preprocessing pipeline for consistent mouth-region representation, a rotational validation strategy for improved generalization to unseen speakers, and a flexible similarity evaluation for more reliable sentence-level assessment. The model architecture combines 3D convolutional layers for spatio-temporal feature extraction and bidirectional recurrent layers for sequence modeling, optimized using the Adam optimizer and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss. On the GRID dataset, LipLingo achieved 95.0\% character-level accuracy (CER 4.99\%) and 87.2\% sentence-level accuracy. At the corpus level, the system obtained a (WER 13.1\%), outperforming the baseline LipNet and demonstrating competitive performance relative to recent 3D-ResNet + Bi-GRU + MixUp approaches. These results provide insights into strategies that enhance lip-reading robustness and highlight directions for future work toward real-world deployment.

Toward Artifact-Free Dermoscopy: Characterization of ISIC 2019 Image Defects for Deep Learning Applications

Toward Artifact-Free Dermoscopy: Characterization of ISIC 2019 Image Defects for Deep Learning Applications

Victoria Wegley、Joshua Hoog、Tristan Crawford、Keith Miller、William Fons 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

The International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) archive offers the largest publicly available collection of dermoscopic images for skin lesion analysis. However, the ISIC 2019 dataset suffers from several acquisition artifacts such as hair occlusions, vignetting, surgical ink markings, and ruler scales, all of which compromise its utility in deep learning workflows by introducing non-biological visual structures. To address these limitations, we present a rigorously annotated version of ISIC 2019 that includes binary masks for key artifact types. Ink marks and vignetting were annotated through systematic manual review and iterative refinement using professional image editing software. For hair and ruler artifacts, we implemented a semi-automatic pipeline based on our previously developed deep learning architecture, ChimeraNet. Automated predictions were then manually corrected as needed for precision. The resulting dataset supports both the development of our own melanoma detection model and broader community research requiring artifact-mitigated dermoscopic images.

Align Once to Explain: Feature Alignment for Scalable B-cosification of Foundational Vision Transformers

Align Once to Explain: Feature Alignment for Scalable B-cosification of Foundational Vision Transformers

Raphael Maser、Siddhartha Gairola、Sukrut Rao、Bernt Schiele

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Foundational vision models have become the de facto standard for many vision tasks due to their strong performance. However, they are notoriously opaque and remain hard to interpret. We present ALOE (ALign Once to Explain), a one-time, label-free feature alignment approach that efficiently converts foundational vision models into inherently interpretable B-cos variants. Once aligned, the B-cos backbone is used as a drop-in replacement across several downstream tasks-amortizing the cost of interpretability. ALOE is robust across pre-training paradigms (supervised, self-supervised, vision-language) and can preserve teacher-level generalization with orders of magnitude less data than training from scratch. On classification, it strongly outperforms vanilla B-cosification (e.g., +10.5 p.p. top-1 on ImageNet for DINOv3 ViT-B/16), retains strong linear probing, k-NN, and zero-shot transfer competitive with foundational backbones (DINOv3, SigLIP2) across diverse downstream datasets. It also preserves spatially structured features useful for dense prediction, while yielding well-localized and highly human-interpretable explanations by design.

Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets

Scaling global tractography with ExaTract: from large cohorts to ultra-high-resolution datasets

Simon Legeay、Felix Matuschke、Bastien Herlin、Jan André Reuter、Christophe Destrieux 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Global tractography offers a theoretical framework for reconstructing white matter connectivity from diffusion MRI by jointly inferring all streamlines and their consistency with the diffusion signal and underlying anatomical priors. However, its sequential nature and log-linear complexity make it computationally prohibitive at the scales demanded by neuroimaging, from large population cohorts such as the Human Connectome Project (HCP) to ex vivo ultra-high-field acquisitions at mesoscopic resolution. In this work, we present ExaTract, a parallelized spin-glass tractography framework designed for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Implemented as an open-source MPI+Kokkos application, ExaTract partitions the tractography domain into spatially overlapping regions processed across distributed memory nodes, with regular synchronization of boundary modifications to preserve global convergence guarantees. We validate ExaTract on both in vivo and ex vivo diffusion MRI data: the complete HCP dataset demonstrates population-scale throughput, while the high-resolution Chenonceau dataset provides the first mesoscopic structural connectome derived from global tractography.

Visual-to-Executable Procedural Reconstruction of Buildings

Visual-to-Executable Procedural Reconstruction of Buildings

Zichong Zhu、Zhihao Liu、Andrei Sharf、Zhanglin Cheng

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Procedural modeling offers compact, editable, and reusable representations for architectural content, but building such models still depends heavily on manually authored grammars. We study image-based procedural building reconstruction from in-the-wild images, with the goal of recovering an executable procedural description that can be instantiated as an editable 3D building asset. Because a single image provides only partial and view-dependent evidence, we focus on recovering the dominant visible facade(s) and attach the recovered facade program to a simple mass model for building-level instantiation. Our method decomposes this task into two structured prediction stages. First, a Global Structure Layout Tree recovers facade-scale split-and-repeat organization through a fine-tuned layout model with render-guided visual-symbolic reflection. Second, a Component Parameterization schema maps representative facade tiles to structured procedural attributes for local architectural component synthesis. These two representations are then deterministically compiled into executable Computer Generated Architecture (CGA) programs, avoiding the brittleness of direct low-level program generation. Experiments show that the proposed framework handles both regular facades and challenging in-the-wild images, while maintaining high structural consistency, procedural executability, and fine-grained architectural detail. The recovered programs further enable controllable and reusable 3D building asset generation.

When Optimization Meets Human Intent: Human-Centered Diffusion Model Optimization

When Optimization Meets Human Intent: Human-Centered Diffusion Model Optimization

Renye Yan、Jikang Cheng

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Diffusion models are evolving from general tools into personalized systems that adapt to user needs through fine-tuning and guidance. However, diffusion optimization mainly targets measurable objectives such as aesthetics, rarely examining whether they align with human intent. Human needs are multidimensional, contextual, and dynamic, whereas existing methods approximate them with fixed metrics. Because these metrics capture human needs only partially and may amplify deviations from true intent during optimization, higher scores need not yield results better matching human expectations. To understand how human needs enter and influence optimization, we systematically analyze how human intent is expressed, translated into optimizable objectives, applied to model behavior or generation, and evaluated through outputs. We further discuss trade-offs affecting human-intent alignment in personalized image generation and gaps between automated metrics and real user judgments. This human-centered synthesis reorganizes diffusion optimization and provides a systematic reference for personalized generation systems designed for human preferences.

Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry

Every Pixel Is an Option: A System One Model for Medical Ultrasound Biometry

Moein Heidari、Junbo Rao、Yudan Chen、Yasamin Medghalchi、River Jiang 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 ⭐ GitHub 开源

**Purpose:** Ultrasound biometry is widely used across various clinical applications, including prenatal and cardiac examinations, to obtain quantitative measurements by placing calipers at anatomical landmarks. However, these measurements remain subject to interoperator variability as they rely largely on manual caliper placement. Conventional methods often use specialized prediction heads for different ultrasound tasks, whereas vision-language models offer flexibility through text instructions. However, direct coordinate prediction does not explicitly model spatial likelihood distributions, limiting the representation of localization ambiguity. **Methods:** We propose Kev-Bio, a vision-language model that uses clinical measurement questions to guide ultrasound landmark detection. Inspired by System One decision models, Kev-Bio uses decision representations of the language model to generate queries for each caliper endpoint. These queries are matched against shared dense ultrasound features to produce spatial probability maps, from which landmark coordinates and clinical measurements are derived. The model is trained end-to-end using both landmark localization and clinical measurement losses. **Results:** On the nine-view FU/GU Biometry 2026 dataset, Kev-Bio achieves a mean radial error (MRE) of 22.50 pixels and a clinical measurement mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.38, outperforming the compared baselines in overall performance. **Conclusion:** These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Kev-Bio for ultrasound landmark detection and clinical measurement across different anatomical views. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/moeinheidari7829/Kev-Bio.

SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning

SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts with Satellite Data using Machine Learning

Ioannis Dravilas、Miruna Stoicescu、Roope Tervo、Carlos Horn、Oriol Hinojo Comellas 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Atmospheric fronts are associated with much of the high-impact weather in the mid-latitudes, yet their identification and classification remain largely manual and subjective. Existing deep learning approaches rely primarily on gridded reanalysis or forecast data, limiting their applicability to satellite observations available for time-critical applications. We introduce SATFRONT, a machine learning framework for detecting cold, warm, and occluded fronts over Europe from geostationary satellite observations, with reanalysis data as an optional additional input. The model is trained on frontal analyses from five European national meteorological services and evaluated against UK Met Office analyses for 2024. Using satellite observations alone, SATFRONT achieves a Critical Success Index (CSI) of 0.428 at a 150 km tolerance, within the range of agreement between analyses from different meteorological services (0.277-0.501) and higher than that of an operational rule-based front detector that uses satellite data (0.133). Adding ERA5 reanalysis increases the CSI to 0.591. ERA5 substantially improves the placement of individual fronts, although its effect on their annual spatial distribution varies by front type. These results demonstrate that cold, warm, and occluded fronts can be detected directly from geostationary satellite observations, providing a basis for automated frontal analyses at the high temporal frequency required for time-critical applications.

End-to-End Stability of Online Active Learning in Large-Scale Neural Systems

End-to-End Stability of Online Active Learning in Large-Scale Neural Systems

Shuiwen Shen、Jinhua Zhang、Chenlei Hou、Peng Shi、Yong Han 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Online Active Learning (OAL) aims to extend deep learning from static inference after offline training to continuous adaptation during real-time interaction with a changing physical environment. This transition is essential for safety-critical applications, but it raises a central theoretical question: whether the online parameter update process remains stable when scaled to multilayer neural architectures. This paper develops a stability-focused OAL framework. The framework uses prediction error as a feedback signal to update a structured deep model, thereby linking online learning with Lyapunov-based energy minimization. We show that prediction error convergence alone is insufficient for global parameter convergence because multilayer networks may admit high-dimensional manifolds of equivalent output solutions. The analysis therefore separates output error regulation, internal zero dynamics, interlayer coupling, and parameter convergence. Persistency of excitation and active damping are then used to remove the residual null-space modes that remain after output error convergence. A cascaded Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic stability of the overall OAL learning process, while monotonic activation functions and diffeomorphic layer mappings provide the uniqueness condition for the target parameter trajectory. The resulting proof provides a theoretical basis for applying online adaptive learning to large-scale neural systems in nonstationary and safety-critical settings.

How to Simplify a Line Chart: A Taxonomy and Feature-Based Evaluation

How to Simplify a Line Chart: A Taxonomy and Feature-Based Evaluation

Rifat Ara Proma、Paul Rosen

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Simplifying large or noisy time-series is often a prerequisite for producing interpretable line charts, yet existing methods vary widely in how they alter visual features such as trends, extrema, periodicity, curvature, roughness, and overall complexity. We introduce a feature-based taxonomy of line chart simplification that evaluates 19 commonly used algorithms across three families: Transformers, Reducers, and Aggregators. We also formalize 12 perceptually motivated, computationally defined visual features commonly used when analyzing time-series in line charts. We assess preservation using multiple similarity metrics per feature to capture different aspects of fidelity, yielding 21 distinct feature-preservation measurements. To capture the trade-off between fidelity and simplicity, we introduce a Feature--Complexity (FC) score that combines feature preservation with complexity. Our systematic evaluation on 80 datasets reveals distinct family-level patterns: Transformers such as Gaussian, Mean, and Median filters achieve A-mode grades on nearly all metrics but retain full temporal resolution; Reducers such as Douglas-Peucker and M4 receive predominantly D-F mode grades trading fidelity for a reduction in the number of rendered points; and Aggregators ASAP and PAA occupy a middle ground with primarily B-C mode grades. We further characterize the predictability of algorithm behavior across datasets: some methods produce consistent grades regardless of dataset type (Gaussian, Mean, Douglas-Peucker), while others exhibit high data-dependency, with performance varying substantially based on dataset characteristics (FPCS, ASAP). An interactive website supporting exploration of all evaluated techniques, datasets, and results is available at https://feature-taxonomy.vercel.app/.

Roz: A Taste Test for World Model Latents

Roz: A Taste Test for World Model Latents

Kenneth Ge、Dhruv Sheth、Kunvar Thaman

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

State of the art latent dynamics world models achieve impressive performance for robot planning. But do they actually encode the physics of the world? In this paper, we show that popular world models today achieve strong results on tasks that reduce to image similarity but forget key details about objects in the scene like mass, deformation, friction, and bounciness. We achieve this by defining precisely what ought to be encoded in such a world model and introducing two new evaluation methods that can directly tease physical properties and easily scale to new ones. Our evaluation, which we call Roz, includes 10 contrastive tasks and 3 continuous tasks, totaling 1734 individual scenarios. We validate our eval on control tasks. On our own model, AnonWM, we find that performance roughly improves with training steps, while not necessarily being correlated with reconstruction MSE. We argue current model failures are a symptom of evaluation strategies (probes and planners) that are opaque, model-specific, and high-compute. Roz requires only a model that can ingest still frames or video, a way to extract latents, and a distance function between them, and it can be run in one pass. We hope future evaluations will adopt Roz's evaluation techniques. More broadly, we hope Roz can be a case study for a future where benchmarks allow rapid iteration and comparison across models.

We argue current model failures are a symptom of evaluation strategies (probes and planners) that are opaque, model-specific, and high-compute. Roz requires only a model that can ingest still frames or video, a way to extract latents, and a distance function between them, and it can be run in one pass. We hope future evaluations will adopt Roz's evaluation techniques. More broadly, we hope Roz can be a case study for a future where benchmarks allow rapid iteration and comparison across models.

Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit

Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit

Zongtan Li、Tianming Liu、Ye Zhao

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Imitation policies inherit the operator's pace, and re-timing the demonstrations to run faster works only until success collapses at two to three times demonstration speed. Recent methods attribute that collapse to distribution shift and answer it with finer rules for which segments may be sped up; we show it has a mechanical cause that segment selection cannot address. A low-level controller realises only a bounded displacement per control period, so merging consecutive commands produces sums outside that bound: training pairs that promise a transition the plant cannot deliver. The share of such pairs in the re-timed data, which we call the exceed share, tracks where the retrained policy collapses. The rule that follows has a single parameter: merge greedily while the sum stays realisable. Every command is then realisable by construction, the demonstrated geometry is preserved, and the speed-up lands only where the demonstrator left slack. On four simulated robomimic tasks, 200 held-out seeds per cell, a merge cap of two is at or above the frozen policy's success on all four, by 14 points on Square, and shortens the successful episodes. At matched tempo, uniform re-timing loses 9 and 16 points on Can and ToolHang, is within noise on the other two, and reaches zero on the hardest at 2x. Placement also matters: no shuffled, entropy-guided or speed-conditioned alternative beats the rule on three of the four tasks, by margins the exceed share alone does not explain; on the fourth, at a tempo the task absorbs, every placement lands in the same band. The same principle carries to a simulated humanoid whole-body tracker: re-timing 429 reference motions within its velocity envelope succeeds on 71% of clips at 2.3x, against 51% for uniform time scaling at 2x.

WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation

WorldSketch: Sketching World Models for Zero-Shot Mobile Manipulation

Jiaming Wang

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Most agentic robotic systems use vision-language models (VLMs) either to orchestrate predefined skills or to directly generate actions, constraints, and control programs. The former is limited by the available skill library, while the latter requires VLMs to reason about precise geometry and contact. In this paper, we propose WorldSketch, a new paradigm for agentic robotics in which a VLM constructs a world model rather than generating robot actions. The VLM acts as an agent that actively queries perception tools to build and visually validate a minimal kinematic world model, capturing only task-relevant objects, their interaction geometry, and possible motions. A geometric planner then jointly optimizes contact and whole-body motion on the resulting model. Moreover, the world model is self-improving: execution feedback verifies outcomes, updates uncertain hypotheses, and enables the agent to revise the model when its predictions are contradicted. We demonstrate the generality of this paradigm across RoboCasa, LIBERO-PRO, and R2R-CE navigation, achieving zero-shot success rates of 91%, 97%, and 76%, respectively. On RoboCasa, WorldSketch outperforms the next-best zero-shot agent baseline by 58 percentage points while using 10 times fewer VLM input tokens; on LIBERO-PRO, it exceeds CaP-X by 82 percentage points. In navigation, it matches the success rate of step-by-step VLM agents while using 6 times fewer input tokens.

Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data

Behavior Graphs: Unsupervised Graph Structures for Interpreting Robot Deployment Data

Erik Bauer、Jakob Thumm、Christopher Agia、Rohan Sinha、Chen Xu 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Data flywheels promise continuous improvement via insights from deployment data. Understanding how the deployed model succeeds and fails can steer subsequent data collection towards patching failures and reinforcing successes. However, robot deployments create large volumes of high-dimensional rollout data, which is challenging to understand and confidently ground data collection decisions in. To make deployment data easier to analyze and act on, we propose behavior graphs, which compress policy rollouts into a single interpretable, directed graph. We construct the graphs by learning to identify similar behavior modes across rollouts, connecting the behaviors temporally, and finally linking them to outcomes. In a user study on three real-world tasks, where participants analyzed rollouts to choose a data collection strategy, 16 of 18 preferred behavior graphs to rollout videos, reaching comparable conclusions with 40.3% lower perceived temporal demand and 37.6% lower effort. Beyond interpretability for deployment data, behavior graphs are capable progress predictors: across 43 datasets, they improve the rank correlation between predicted progress and true temporal order by 22.9% and reduce mean absolute error by 53.5% relative to the strongest baseline. As the number of deployed robots grows, behavior graphs lend structure to high-dimensional policy rollouts and make deployment data easier to interpret and reason about.

CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports

CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports

Joey Guo、Rayan Ansari、Alaa Youssef

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promise for chest radiograph report generation, but adoption remains limited because of hallucinated findings that are not grounded in the image. Correcting these hallucinations and improving overall report quality remains a significant challenge. Prior work has addressed this problem by refining models with reinforcement learning, preference optimization, or chain-of-thought supervision, often at substantial compute cost. To address this gap, we introduce CheXPoT, a program-of-thought (PoT) framework that verifies each generated finding against image features and removes those it cannot ground. CheXPoT decomposes generated reports into predicates with RadGraph and an LLM, grounds these predicates against a DenseNet-121 and Grad-CAM visual evidence table, executes PoT verification code, and rewrites reports after removing unsupported predicates. On a 4,145-image held-out split, CheXPoT yields statistically significant precision gains on 8 of 14 CheXpert classes and F1 gains on 5, with no significant decreases in either metric. CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 19.2% (MedGemma-4B) to 46.8% (MedGemma-4B + CheXPoT) and micro-average F1 from 23.0% to 49.4%, absolute gains of 27.6% and 26.4% respectively. We also tested CheXPoT on other VLM report generators. On LLaVA-Med, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 4.5% to 17.7% and micro-average F1 from 6.3% to 19.4%. On MAIRA-2, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 15.6% to 42.1% and micro-average F1 from 21.0% to 45.3%. Our results suggest that inexpensive post-hoc visual verification may improve VLM trustworthiness by correcting unsupported findings from generated reports. CheXPoT lays a foundation for tools that help validate VLM-generated radiology reports and reduce unsupported findings. These innovations may subsequently help increase trust and adoption of VLM tools in Medicine.

STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving

STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving

Yangang Zou、Pei Liu、Nan Song、Bozhou Zhang、Mingyu Guo 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Vision-language action (VLA) models excel for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet their tendency to over-invoke chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mirrors a human cognitive pitfall: overthinking. Just as deliberate reasoning can slow or mislead human judgment in routine tasks, excessive CoT in VLA incurs unnecessary compute overhead and can paradoxically degrade planning performance. Recent research tackles this via adaptive reasoning, which dynamically modulates inference complexity by selectively triggering CoT for complex scenes while responding directly to routine ones. While prior adaptive methods rely on implicit adaptation, recent work shows that explicitly optimizing the route between CoT and direct responses yields superior performance, assuming scene-difficulty annotations which are labor-intensive, poorly scalable, and prone to error due to the subjectivity of judging driving complexity. We explore, for the first time, whether adaptive reasoning with explicit route optimization can be achieved without any scene-difficulty labeling. We introduce STEER, a generic over-reasoning mitigation strategy featuring two key components: (i) routing uncertainty-aware rollout, which calibrates sampling to align routing diversity with model uncertainty; and (ii) cross-route advantage credit assignment, which introduces a differential metric to reinforce optimal routing decisions based on environmental rewards rather than subjective labels. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 demonstrate that STEER is competitive with state-of-the-art methods in both planning quality and the Pareto front of inference efficiency.

$TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering

$TF^2$-Steering: Action Refinement with Tactile Forecasts and Feedback via Velocity-Field Steering

Yiming Chen、Xiaofei Wei、Chun Gu、Wei Xiao、Peidong Liu 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Tactile sensing plays a crucial role in everyday human interaction. Consider inserting a plug into a tight socket, vision alone provides limited guidance during the final insertion stage, and we instead rely on both anticipated contact and realized tactile feedback to ajust the insertion motion. The same capability is equally important for robots, particularly in dexterous manipulation tasks. Yet many contemporary robot policies remain vision-dominant. This visual bias, compounded by limited tactile data and sparse contact events, can cause directly incorporated tactile signals to be ignored or even compromise the policy's pretrained capabilities, yielding degrading performance as observed in our experiments. We present $TF^2$-Steering, which refines actions via learned residual steering of the flow-matching action expert's velocity field, using a tactile mixture-of-experts architecture to integrate both tactile forecasts and real-time tactile feedback. Together with specific designed three stages training recipe, $TF^2$-Steering enables tactile signals to correct and, when necessary, redirect the flow-matching action-generation process, while building on the strong action-generation capacity of the vision-based foundation policy. Extensive experiments across six simulated and six real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of $TF^2$-Steering. It outperforms the strongest evaluated baselines by 10.7 percentage points in average simulation success rate and 9.1 percentage points in average real-world progress success rate. Project page: https://yiming-cc.github.io/tf2-steering/.

FOCUS: Closed-Loop Attention Feedback for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding

FOCUS: Closed-Loop Attention Feedback for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding

Akul Santhosh、Aastha Jhunjhunwala

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Processing every video frame through Vision-Language Models (VLMs) adds significant inference cost and limits their ability to comprehend real-time video. Existing approaches either sub-sample frames uniformly, ignoring content and missing important events, or prune visual tokens inside the VLM to cut per-call cost while still invoking the model on every sampled frame. We introduce FOCUS, a training-free three-layer framework that reduces the number of invocations and steers each one towards what matters. Temporal gating measures inter-frame dissimilarity in the patch-embedding space of a smaller VLM from the same family, triggering burst captures only when the scene changes in a semantically meaningful way. Patch-level dissimilarity is then accumulated across the burst and fused with a top-down attention prior into a spatial focus map that encodes where motion and semantic relevance coincide. That map calibrates the VLM's value cache during generation, progressively amplifying vision tokens in task-relevant regions and attenuating off-target ones, without removing any token from the context. The loop closes after each response: text-to-vision cross-attention is extracted from the decoder and fed back as the prior for the next burst, letting the system converge on semantically important regions over successive observations. We evaluate FOCUS on the 500-video EgoSchema subset in streaming mode, with a single Qwen3-VL-8B backbone shared by every method. It reaches 74.8% accuracy using 25.4 VLM calls per clip, against 74.6% with 55 calls for uniform sampling and 74.2% with 55 calls for BOLT. On egocentric video captioning across four domains, it matches the best baseline's quality while issuing 57% fewer VLM invocations than uniform sampling.

Serving Agentic Robot Fleets: Workload Characterization, KV-Cache Thrashing, and Admission Control

Serving Agentic Robot Fleets: Workload Characterization, KV-Cache Thrashing, and Admission Control

Sida He

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Agentic robots combine a vision-language brain, a tool-using harness, and a vision-language-action (VLA) policy. Serving a fleet of these agents introduces two coupled resource constraints: the brain repeatedly revisits long, growing key-value (KV) cache states, while the VLA executes action chunks under tight control deadlines. We characterize 80 LIBERO-PRO episodes generated by GPT-6-Astra, RPent, and pi0.5 (1,862 brain turns and 1,582 VLA inference chunks), profile both layers on H800 graphics processing units (GPUs), and replay the resulting agent programs on a vLLM serving engine. Brain contexts reach 215k tokens; the median Astra request takes 7.78 s, while the intervening environment-step gap is only 1.0 s. Under a 0.25 s action-chunk deadline, one VLA GPU meets the 1% starvation target for one robot; under a 1.0 s deadline, its measured capacity reaches at least 32. In sustained brain replay, increasing concurrency from 20 to 32 robots reduces throughput from about 2.4 to 0.6 requests/s as repetitive prefill displaces generation. A static active-episode cap restores 2.24-2.25 requests/s and raises completed trace-program throughput from 1.30 to 5.00-5.55 episodes/min. Our measurements expose the workload-dependent shift between action deadlines and brain KV residency, and establish practical principles for capacity planning and admission in sustained agentic robot fleets.

Trading Transparency for Stability: Friction-Cone-Constrained Bilateral Teleoperation for Opening Doors of Unsecured Furniture

Trading Transparency for Stability: Friction-Cone-Constrained Bilateral Teleoperation for Opening Doors of Unsecured Furniture

Cheng Zhou、Jing Li

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Opening the door of unsecured furniture loads the frictional contacts at its supports; too large a pull slides or tips the object. A friction-cone constraint on the commanded wrench removes this failure mode but costs haptic transparency. We quantify the trade-off: an admissible wrench set built from contact friction cones and support-polygon tipping margins is shrunk for robustness to bounded mass and friction errors, and any command in the shrunken set provably leaves the furniture static (Prop. 1). We call this map the robust friction cone projection (RFCP). RFCP and its haptic guard admit a bounded force transmission error (Prop. 2): transparency degrades only within a band near the constraint boundary, whose width is set by one scalar, the stability factor . A working condition controller handles the door: the operator commands a scalar swing amplitude, the slave orientation follows hinge kinematics, and the grasp wrench is regulated per phase. A pre task certificate decides whether a door can be opened without moving the furniture. Experiments on three cabinets and two supports with five operators (100 trials) measure the stability transparency trade-off and ablate the guard, RFCP and the position baseline. The mechanism is not door-specific: it applies to any body reacted by frictional contacts.

Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection

Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection

Eshaq Jamdar、Amith Kamath Belman

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Many Automated Speaker Verification Systems (ASVs) commonly employ liveliness detection techniques, such as VoicePop, which identify genuine speech by analyzing low- frequency pop bursts from plosive phonemes using Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCC) and an SVM classifier. While effective against traditional replay attacks, such systems are vulnerable to data poisoning techniques. Prior work shows that broadly applied SyntheticPop attacks can collapse model to accuracy to as low as 14.01% using only 20% poisoned samples, but the resulting artifacts are easily detectable when visualizing the waveform energies. This paper introduces Pop Goes the Verifier, a stealthier phoneme injection poisoning attack. By leveraging FastSpeech 2 (FS2) with a modified HiFi-GAN vocoder, we inject localized pop bursts at plosive phoneme locations and overlay subtle Gaussian noise to reduce the visibility of injected artifacts in waveform and spectrogram analysis. Using the ASVSpoof 2019 as the dataset, we observe that the approach achieves a moderate poisoning attack while providing greater resistance to signal-level inspection than the original SyntheticPop attack.

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

No algorithm is best on all problems, but a real warehouse is a narrow problem: its layout and processes rarely change. Operators still run one general multi-robot planner at many sites, because experts cannot tune it for each one. In this work, which we call Late Autumn, we explore whether LLM coding agents running autonomous research can specialize a general planner for one site, trading generality for throughput, much as post-training adapts a pretrained LLM to one task. We study six campaigns on a lifelong planner that combines task assignment with multi-agent path finding, on a floor modeled on an existing automated warehouse. We find that (1) the agents raise throughput by 22--60%, and the gains hold on unseen seeds; (2) they rediscover known MAPF mechanisms, such as corridor-exit priorities, local guidance, and rollouts, and independent campaigns find the same bottleneck; (3) the gains largely carry over to another layout, a larger fleet, and other service times, shrink with a smaller fleet, and mostly vanish under an outbound-heavy demand mix; and (4) each final patch (0.7k--2.4k lines) is a chain of scored commits with a median step of 27 lines, so experts can review it, and review finds problems that the score misses; some patches multiply planner compute by over 100x. LLM agents can therefore turn each site's bias into extra throughput at little engineering cost, with reviewable patches; we expect experts to shift toward designing insightful metrics and fast simulators that mirror the real problem.

When to Probe and When to Act: Clarity-Aware Risk-Adaptive Control for Interactive Driving

When to Probe and When to Act: Clarity-Aware Risk-Adaptive Control for Interactive Driving

Youran Wang、Devodita Chakravarty、Yiwei Lyu

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Safe navigation in interactive traffic requires autonomous vehicles to reason about unobservable human characteristics and the reciprocal nature of multi-agent interactions. Traditional architectures often decouple prediction from planning, leading to the "Frozen Robot Problem" or unsafe maneuvers under high ambiguity because they treat risk assessment and information acquisition as independent objectives. We argue that the notion of safety should not remain static but must instead dynamically co-evolve with the system's internal confidence: the robot should actively clarify ambiguity when necessary while also recognizing the diminishing returns of information, and naturally transition toward task execution. We introduce a unified belief-space Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework that couples multistep information planning with a clarity-adaptive Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) barrier mechanism. By treating clarity, a scalar informational state, as an explicit planning variable, the controller co-designs its probing strategy with its safety specification, tightening conservatism under high ambiguity and relaxing constraints as confidence improves. We further provide a performance analysis showing that the cost of information seeking and the expected planning-cost gap to a controller that knows the true human characteristic are bounded by residual ambiguity and solver error. We evaluate the framework in lane-merging and unsignalized-intersection scenarios against representative interactive-planning baselines. Across 5,000 simulations, the proposed method achieves the highest success rates (94.6% and 93.2%) and the lowest collision rates (1.2% and 1.4%) among the compared methods, providing a principled foundation for robust decision-making in human-centric environments.

Directional Bounded-Confidence Matrix Alignment in Vicsek Flocking

Directional Bounded-Confidence Matrix Alignment in Vicsek Flocking

Hossein B. Jond

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

This paper proposes a directional bounded-confidence variant of the discrete-time Vicsek multiagent model, in which pairwise heading alignment is modulated by a state-dependent, positive semidefinite matrix that independently gates orthogonal radial and tangential components in the instantaneous line-of-sight frame. We analyze the normalized, matrix-weighted system dynamics, proving a uniform non-vanishing bound on proposal vectors that guarantees global well-posedness across arbitrary network states. For local small-spread states under complete metric interaction, we prove linear geometric contraction of the heading diameter and establish an offline-verifiable spatial bootstrap condition that guarantees metric contact preservation and coincidence avoidance a priori. A counterexample demonstrates invariant polarized states on connected matrix graphs, delineating systemic structural limits. Numerical experiments against unfiltered Vicsek averaging, scalar tied confidence, trace-matched scalar baselines, and restricted-angle rules demonstrate component-selective filtering without rejected-channel leakage, along with improved fixed-bound alignment on multi-seed benchmarks across varying population densities.

Human Sensorimotor Model Adaptation to Account for Robot Accuracy and Speed Augmentation in Human-Robot Co-Manipulation

Human Sensorimotor Model Adaptation to Account for Robot Accuracy and Speed Augmentation in Human-Robot Co-Manipulation

Frits van Hall、Kevin Haninger、Luka Peternel

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

In human-robot co-manipulation, the robot's trajectory should accommodate the human's, where human sensorimotor behavior is affected by the task's spatial and temporal constraints, as well as personal factors. Several robot trajectory planning methods have been proposed to embed human sensorimotor models in the robot trajectory planning, but these methods do not consider temporal constraints that adapt to how the human behaves when interacting with the robot. To better align human and robot collaborative motion, this work adapts a stochastic optimal control problem with a final state constraint from the task constraints and a temporal constraint from Fitts' law. A recursive least squares method is used to estimate the Fitts' law parameters, adapting the robot's motion duration to that of the human, thus allowing the robot to adapt to how the human behaves when interacting with the robot. It is hypothesized that a speed increase can result from the robot augmenting the accuracy. The feasibility of the approach is validated on a positioning task where the robot controls degrees of freedom which have repeatable motion, and the human adapts motion in the complementary degrees of freedom. The approach is shown to be computationally suited to online use, it converges as the human and robot mutually adapt, and can increase the movement speed, although thorough human studies are needed in future work.

GoalDex: Learning Image-Goal-Conditioned Policies for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

GoalDex: Learning Image-Goal-Conditioned Policies for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

Arjun Bhardwaj、Mayank Mittal、Maximum Wilder-Smith、Vaishakh Patil、Marco Hutter 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Dexterous in-hand manipulation is commonly formulated around explicit object pose estimation, yet reliable pose tracking is challenging under severe hand-object occlusions and often requires object-specific supervision. This dependence creates a bottleneck between perception and control that can limit robustness and scalability. We present an end-to-end visuomotor framework for dexterous in-hand reorientation that operates on RGB observations and proprioception without intermediate pose estimation. Our approach jointly learns visual representations and control policies through behavior distillation from privileged state teachers and auxiliary reconstruction objectives. Furthermore, we introduce image-goal-conditioned reorientation, allowing desired object configurations to be specified directly through images rather than canonical pose representations. We evaluate our approach across a diverse set of object geometries and instances in simulation, where it consistently outperforms pose-based methods and policies built on pretrained visual encoders. Finally, we demonstrate direct sim-to-real transfer of a single image-goal-conditioned policy across five real-world objects, showing that accurate dexterous reorientation can be achieved without explicit pose estimation. For videos and code release, please refer to the project website: https://rffr.leggedrobotics.com/works/goaldex/

Infinite Worlds from One Example: What Local Generators Must Share

Infinite Worlds from One Example: What Local Generators Must Share

Amin Najafgholizadeh、Mohsen Afsharchi

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Seeded noise lets games generate any region of an unbounded world on demand. We ask what such a generator needs when every small window must come from one example, the constraint behind Wave Function Collapse. The difficulty is that local constraints can require agreement over arbitrary distances: in a brick wall, each row keeps its place between the mortar lines. We study local generators, each cell a fixed function of the randomness near it. When the constraints carry a quantity that varies across the example, no generator that applies one rule, ignoring position, to independent randomness at every cell can be both exactly valid and faithful to the example's statistics, however far each cell reads. At radius r, staying faithful forces forbidden windows at a density of at least order 1/r, and a construction attains this order. To vary the quantity between exactly valid worlds, a generator needs randomness shared along its direction. We give a finitely checkable condition under which row types drawn from the seed and the position modulo a fixed period suffice for exact validity without learning. A search over the example's patches certifies these quantities and names the input each needs. Across 52 public examples of Wave Function Collapse and 27 from other implementations, it certifies only examples where a learned generator on independent randomness stays far from valid after repair. Given that input, a neural cellular automaton and a diffusion model become valid on 10 and 8 of the 12 certified examples that receive one, and on none from independent randomness. Valid means at most one forbidden window in a thousand after repair. With octaves of seeded noise elsewhere, the automaton is valid on 45 of the 52 public examples and 21 of the 27 from other implementations, and repair keeps random access.

CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control

CompliantBot: Learning Whole-Body Compliance across Task Interfaces for Humanoid Control

Haoyang Li、Keqi Zhu、Zhanxiang Cao、Yang Zhang、Yizhi Chen 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Humanoid controllers need the ability to yield to external forces while retaining the capacity to resume their original tasks. However, tracking objectives penalize the deviations needed for yielding, while relaxing tracking goals persistently can make task recovery harder. Existing approaches often rely on task-specific interaction command interfaces or constructed compliant motion data and reference trajectories, limiting the direct reuse of their compliance-training mechanisms across different task interfaces. We introduce CompliantBot, a compliance-training framework for motion tracking and velocity-command locomotion. It preserves the original task inputs and requires no preconstructed compliant data or target trajectories. A state-dependent interaction force field couples applied loads to the robot's motion, enabling local articulation and whole-body movement to change the forces experienced. A complementary force-magnitude reward encourages lower interaction loads, while task rewards are downweighted during loading and restored after release to coordinate yielding and task resumption. The trained policies use task inputs and proprioceptive history without explicit external-force measurements. Across both task interfaces, CompliantBot yields farther under constant pulls and experiences lower spring interaction loads than matched baselines, while resuming task tracking after force removal. CompliantBot achieves the highest task completion among the compared methods under stronger pulls. Power evaluations further show that CompliantBot has the lowest mean joint mechanical power among the compared methods. Real-robot demonstrations further illustrate compliant responses through arm motion, stepping, and body reorientation.

Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning

Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning

Zixi Yi、Gary P. T. Choi

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.

Swarm Choreography Made Simple: Superposed Guiding Vector Fields for Rigid Formation Path Following

Swarm Choreography Made Simple: Superposed Guiding Vector Fields for Rigid Formation Path Following

Jo{ã}o Machado、Matthieu Verdoucq、Christophe Jouffrais、Murat Bronz

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

This paper presents a decentralized guiding vector field framework for rigid formation path following in multi- UAV systems based on the superposition of simple rule-driven vector fields. Each control objective is encoded as a dedicated vector-field component: a normalized tangential term to ensure progression along a prescribed geometric path at a desired speed, a convergence term driving the formation toward the path, a local coordination term that preserves the desired formation shape through a pseudo-path parameter, and a local separation term for inter-agent collision avoidance. The coordination mechanism requires the exchange of only a single scalar per agent, resulting in low communication bandwidth. Partial theoretical results establish convergence of the swarm to the desired path and formation in the absence of the sepa- ration term, while collision avoidance is formally guaranteed. The approach is experimentally validated using a swarm of five quadrotors executing two 3D choreographies. The first experiment involves tracking a helical path while maintaining a rigid V-shaped formation. The second demonstrates a spiral- like motion obtained by a rotating circular formation tracking a vertical line. The experimental results support the effectiveness and practical applicability of the proposed framework.

RESONATE: a Real Social Navigation Testbed for Autonomous Service Robots

RESONATE: a Real Social Navigation Testbed for Autonomous Service Robots

Stefano Trepella、Andrea Ostuni、Mauro Martini、Irene Borgini、Marcello Chiaberge 等

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Social navigation is essential for autonomous service robots operating in human environments, but progress remains constrained by the lack of extensive real-world benchmarks. This paper presents the Real Social Navigation Testbed (RESONATE), a reproducible benchmark for human-aware navigation based on a unified robotic platform, a shared ROS 2 software stack, precise trajectory ground truth, and structured social interaction scenarios. We evaluate eight controller configurations, combining classical and predictive local planners with different social modeling strategies, over eight representative scenarios with five repetitions each, yielding 320 physical experiments. The benchmark combines quantitative navigation and social metrics with participant-based qualitative assessments to jointly measure efficiency, safety, comfort, and perceived social behavior. Results reveal scenario-dependent trade-offs among the tested methods. The algorithms that stands out for their performance are the DWA with Gaussian social costmaps for its reliability, and the SFM-MPPI to provide the best balance between robustness, navigation efficiency, and social acceptance. Overall, RESONATE supports the robotics community with a real-world benchmark, reusable baselines, data, and testbed, and a consistent evaluation protocol for advancing socially aware navigation research.

An intelligent satellite must do nothing well

An intelligent satellite must do nothing well

Fabrizio Pilone、Giordana Bucchioni

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Autonomous inspection of a resident space object is usually posed as a contest between classical next-best-view planning and reinforcement learning. We argue that the choice of algorithm is the least informative of the design axes. An inspector spacecraft has no rest state: when it stops thrusting, orbital dynamics carry it along a natural trajectory that can be used to observe the target at no fuel cost. On a controlled ladder in which one design axis is varied at a time, fuel efficiency turns out to be set by three things: whether the agent is allowed to drift, whether its state records where drifting has taken it, and whether its planning horizon is long enough for the benefit to appear. Removing any one of them doubles the fuel bill or more. The algorithm still matters, but through what it can represent: a model-based agent whose learned world model ignores fuel spends several times more of it. Finally, no learned policy is safe by construction, and a control barrier function filter beneath the decision layer removed every keep-out-zone violation in two thousand evaluation episodes.

Right Ranking, Wrong Scale: Reproducing the Robotic World Model's Dynamics Model and Testing the Uncertainty of Its Follow-up

Joyjeet Singh

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

We reimplement the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) and test the uncertainty estimate that its follow-up, RWM-U, uses to penalize reward in offline policy optimization. Our implementation matches the released model's gradients. On held-out data, training on the model's own rollouts beats one-step training at the preregistered long horizon for all ten episodes, but loses on short one-step windows. RWM-U's ensemble disagreement ranks rollout errors better than forecast step (Spearman rho = 0.90 at 100 steps), yet its spread substantially understates error: one-sigma coverage on the released checkpoint is 4.6% at 100 steps, versus 68% for a calibrated Gaussian. Rolling ensemble members on their own predictions raises coverage to 33%. The implemented squared-error loss on sampled predictions drives each member's variance toward zero. A horizon-specific rescaling restores one-sigma coverage under leave-one-episode-out evaluation, but not two-sigma coverage. We also identify two defects in the released evaluation pipeline. The study covers one robot, one gait and one dataset; it trains no policy.

The study covers one robot, one gait and one dataset; it trains no policy.

Recent advances in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have enabled fine manipulation capabilities, yet performing tasks that require working memory remains a key challenge. Most existing VLA architectures operate under a Markovian assumption, mapping only the current observation to an action, which leads to failure in non-Markovian environments. Inspired by the human 'inner monologue', we propose Hierarchical Explicit Language Memory (HeLM), a hierarchical VLA framework that maintains task-relevant history in explicit language through factorized event detection and event-triggered memory updates. We evaluate HeLM across 10 non-Markovian real-world tasks with 56 variants, including five newly formulated inter-episode tasks that require persistent context across task boundaries. HeLM improves intra-episode success by 12.8 percentage points over the strongest baseline and achieves 78% subtask success on compositional generalization tasks, while using up to 4.5x less memory and running 2.5x faster than the keyframe baseline at long horizons.

Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants

Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants

Giuseppe Silano

论文页面 PDF HTML 版本 暂无开源

Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.
